Speedy Stockers Duel for
Lead
*
*
RUSS LAKE PHOTO
PACKER PONTIAC
*
*
DICK JOHNSON PHOTO
Two memorable battles for the lead occurred in the July 15 200 mile late model stock car race here at
state fair park. First, Don White, Keokuk, Ia. (#4-1962 Zecol-Lubaid Ford) roared past A. J. Foyt, Houston, Tex.
(#7-Nichels Engineering Pontiac) on the 14th mile. Foyt had led from the first turn but could not stave off
White's challenges. White came on to win the race.
White later was pressed by Paul Goldsmith, St, Clair Shores, Mich. (#1 - 1962 Nichels Engineering Pontiac)
who went into the lead. Goldsmith then found himself challenged by Norm Nelson, Racine, Wis. (#2 - 1962
Wynn Oil Ford) as both are seen lapping Mike Klapak, Warren, Ohio (#52 - 1962 Ford) near the 80 mile mark.
Goldsmith fought off Nelson until both came to the pits for gas on the 100th mile. Nelson then led until the
197 mile when he was forced in again for gas. Goldsmith burned a valve on his car and drove to finish the
race, coming in fifth.

BAY DARNELL
Deerfield, III.
Bay Darnell made his first appearance in a
national championship late model stock car race
here in the July 15 200 miler and finished a credit-
able 14th. Has competed in several races on the
United States Auto Club late model circuit this
summer. Bay is no stranger to Milwaukee fans
having raced here many times in modified stock
cars and has scored one feature race victory.
NEIL HOUSTON
Des Plaines, III.
Likeable Neil Houston had rough going in the
July 15 200 mile stock car race here but still
managed to finish 20th. Was running in the first
10 until he was involved in a two car spin with
Troy Ruttman of Dearborn, Mich. on the 47th
mile. Ruttman's car was out for the day. Houston
had his car inspected and approved and went back
into the race. One of the few drivers in racing to
wear a goatee.
